title: Transformers
overview: Transformers replace recurrence with self-attention, letting every token attend to every other token in parallel. They underpin most modern language, vision and multimodal models.
objectives: Explain multi-head attention and positional information
Describe a transformer block and masking

method.title: Self-attention
method.body: Each token produces a query, key and value; attention = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d)) V.

method.title: Multi-head
method.body: Several attention heads in parallel let the model capture different relations, then outputs are concatenated and projected.

method.title: Position
method.body: Attention is order-agnostic, so positional encodings or embeddings inject sequence order.

method.title: Block
method.body: Each block applies attention and a feed-forward network, each wrapped with residual connections and layer norm.

method.title: Masking
method.body: A causal mask blocks attention to future tokens for autoregressive generation.

pseudocode:
Q, K, V = x @ Wq, x @ Wk, x @ Wv
scores = Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)
scores += causal_mask   # optional
out = softmax(scores) @ V
x = x + out @ Wo
x = x + ffn(layer_norm(x))

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
T, d = 4, 8
x = rng.normal(size=(T, d))
Wq, Wk, Wv = (rng.normal(size=(d, d)) * 0.3 for _ in range(3))
Q, K, V = x @ Wq, x @ Wk, x @ Wv
scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(d)
scores += np.triu(np.full((T, T), -1e9), k=1)  # causal mask
w = np.exp(scores - scores.max(-1, keepdims=True))
w /= w.sum(-1, keepdims=True)
print(np.round(w, 2))
print("output shape:", (w @ V).shape)

quiz.question: Why divide attention scores by sqrt(d_k)?
options: To reduce the number of heads
To keep dot products from growing too large before softmax
